item.title: 11 of 14 water sources reach critical levels in Western Division as Govt steps up drought response
item.description: 11 of the 14 water sources have reached critical levels in the Western Division, with the Government intensifying its response to the ongoing El Niño drought. The Vaturu Dam reservoir has also dropped below its critical level of 522 metres.
item.content:encoded:
11 of the 14 water sources have reached critical levels in the Western Division, with the Government intensifying its response to the ongoing El Niño drought.

The Vaturu Dam reservoir has also dropped below its critical level of 522 metres.

Commissioner Western Apolosi Lewaqai says emergency operation centres have been activated across districts to coordinate assistance and monitor communities affected by the worsening water shortage.

He says the Government has allocated $20 million from existing ministerial budgets to support the national drought response.

This includes the deployment of 39 water trucks to areas served by metered water supplies, as well as emergency water deliveries to Yasawa, Malolo and Vatulele.

Lewaqai says priority is being given to families and communities facing severe water shortages.

He adds that relevant agencies are continuing to assess the impact of the drought on agriculture, livestock, fisheries and public health.

Lewaqai is also urging organisers of community events to consider postponing their activities to reduce pressure on limited water supplies.

Meanwhile, contingency measures, including possible water and electricity rationing, are being considered if conditions worsen.

However, no decision on rationing has been announced.

Members of the public are being urged to conserve water and avoid unnecessary wastage.

item.title: Young boy's quick action leads to discovery of suspicious package in Lakeba
item.description: Pita Toganivalu , Temalesi Vono · 24/11/2026 A young boy from Oneata, Lau, who was with his father in Lakeba, has been praised for alerting his family after discovering a suspicious package at sea.
item.content:encoded:
Pita Toganivalu , Temalesi Vono · 24/11/2026

A young boy from Oneata, Lau, who was with his father in Lakeba, has been praised for alerting his family after discovering a suspicious package at sea.

Sikeli Tokaduadua says he found the package, initially thinking it contained money, and alerted his father, who later reported the discovery to Police.

The contents of the package have yet to be confirmed.

Tokaduadua says he took the package home and showed it to his father.

His father then took the package to the village headman (Tui Soso).

His father, Josefa Vukimawi, says he has been working in Lakeba for almost four years.

Vukimawi says his son knew what to do because Ministry officials have conducted drug awareness programmes on the island.

He adds that he also noticed something unusual while out fishing about two weeks ago.

He says he saw two fibreglass boats floating alongside a yacht.

Vukimawai says when they noticed he was coming near, the yacht moved while the two fibreglass boats moved away.

He says this could be connected to what his son discovered, although any link between the two observations has yet to be confirmed.

Villagers are being reminded not to touch or approach suspicious packages or unfamiliar objects found at sea or along the shoreline.

People are advised to move away, inform a trusted adult and report the discovery to the Fiji Police Force.

The Ministry of Policing says it acknowledges the boy and his family for acting quickly and doing the right thing.

It says maritime security begins with empowered coastal communities, where people know what to look for and understand the importance of reporting suspicious activities.

Anyone who sees something suspicious can contact Police on 1681 or visit their nearest Police Station.

item.title: Eight people, including a child, left homeless after Nadi house fire
item.description: Eight people, including a child, have been left homeless after a fire destroyed their two-flat home at Bila Settlement in Waqadra, Nadi, on Sunday. The National Fire Authority (NFA) says the eight adults and one child managed to escape safely before the fire completely destroyed the corrugated iron and timber residential building.
item.content:encoded:
Eight people, including a child, have been left homeless after a fire destroyed their two-flat home at Bila Settlement in Waqadra, Nadi, on Sunday.

The National Fire Authority (NFA) says the eight adults and one child managed to escape safely before the fire completely destroyed the corrugated iron and timber residential building.

NFA says arriving at the scene six minutes later, they found the building fully engulfed in flames.

The property sustained 100 percent structural damage, including its contents, with the total loss provisionally estimated at $150,000.

NFA Chief Executive Officer Puamau Sowane says the incident highlights how quickly a fire can spread and destroy a home.

Sowane is urging families to take fire prevention seriously, ensure their homes have appropriate fire safety measures and have an emergency evacuation plan in place.

NFA will conduct an investigation to establish the suspected cause of the fire.

Members of the public are reminded to call 910 in the event of a fire or emergency.

item.title: Methodist Church encourages ministers to abstain from kava and smoking ahead of National Week of Prayer
item.description: The Methodist Church in Fiji will be holding a National Week of Prayer, Fasting and Consecration from the 1st to the 7th of December, with all ministers encouraged to abstain from drinking kava and smoking as the Church prepares for the important occasion. As part of the programme, selected Methodist churches will open their doors to members of the public for midday prayer services from 12 noon to
item.content:encoded:
The Methodist Church in Fiji will be holding a National Week of Prayer, Fasting and Consecration from the 1st to the 7th of December, with all ministers encouraged to abstain from drinking kava and smoking as the Church prepares for the important occasion.

As part of the programme, selected Methodist churches will open their doors to members of the public for midday prayer services from 12 noon to 1pm.

The designated locations are Suva, Nausori, Wesley, Lautoka, Nadi, Namoli, Macuata/Nasea and Savusavu/Savusavu Town.

The instruction was emphasised by Methodist Church President Reverend Dr Semisi Turagavou in an announcement outlining additional preparations for the national programme.

Reverend Turagavou is calling on all ministers to recognise their spiritual responsibilities on behalf of the nation.

He says ministers are expected to dedicate themselves fully to prayer, fasting and consecration as they prepare for the national programme.

All divisional superintendents have also been urged to make the necessary spiritual and practical preparations, with the Church saying the initiative requires full commitment, dedication and leadership.

The prayer sessions will be open to everyone, regardless of religious affiliation, giving members of the public an opportunity to come together and pray for Fiji.

Reverend Turagavou is also calling on ministers, church leaders and Church members to take these instructions seriously as the nation prepares for the week of prayer, fasting and consecration.

The Methodist Church says the programme is an opportunity for Fijians to stand together in prayer and seek God's guidance, protection and blessings upon the nation.

item.title: Families in Naitasiri urged to take precautions as bull sharks enter rivers during breeding season
item.description: Families in Naitasiri who rely on rivers for bathing, fishing and other daily activities are being urged to take extra precautions as bull sharks are expected to move into Fiji's rivers during their breeding season. The Ministry of Fisheries has issued the warning following a recent shark incident in Naitasiri, where a man was injured.
item.content:encoded:
Families in Naitasiri who rely on rivers for bathing, fishing and other daily activities are being urged to take extra precautions as bull sharks are expected to move into Fiji's rivers during their breeding season.

The Ministry of Fisheries has issued the warning following a recent shark incident in Naitasiri, where a man was injured.

The Ministry has expressed concern for the injured man and his family, while stressing that investigations are still underway and people should avoid making assumptions about the incident.

They say bull sharks are commonly found in rivers across Naitasiri, including the Wainimala and Waidina rivers, as they can survive in both saltwater and freshwater.

The sharks can swim many kilometres upstream, with confirmed sightings and catches recorded as far inland as Vunidawa.

The Ministry says female bull sharks usually move from coastal waters into rivers between December and February to give birth.

They say young sharks remain in shallow, muddy waters, where they are protected from larger predators while they grow.

Research by the University of the South Pacific has also confirmed the presence of bull sharks in Fiji's river systems, including the Rewa, Navua and Sigatoka rivers.

The Ministry says while the presence of sharks in rivers is normal during this period, attacks on people are extremely rare.

However, families are being advised to avoid swimming or bathing in muddy water, particularly after heavy rain or flooding, when visibility is poor.

People are also being warned against swimming near areas where fish are being cleaned, fish waste is dumped or fishing nets are being used, as these activities can attract sharks.

Parents and guardians are urged to closely supervise children near river mouths and other areas where sharks may be present.

The Ministry is also encouraging communities to report unusual shark sightings to the relevant authorities.

They say people should remain alert rather than fearful, as sharks play an important role in keeping river and coastal ecosystems healthy.

The Ministry will continue monitoring shark sightings and working with relevant organisations to raise awareness and improve public safety.
